issue_context.title: Allow asset loaders to call other asset loaders - the "gzip" problem
issue_context.body:
The feature request is simple: Process one asset and pass it to the next asset loader.

This should be possible:
- Asset loader exists for extensions "gz", "tar.gz"
- Asset loader decompresses the asset
- Asset loader sends to the next asset loader

In example:
I have a "my_image.svg.gz", which I want to be ungzipped, before my svg asset loader takes it.
comments:
I am also interested in this as right now its not really possible to load an asset package that combines multiple assets into a single file.

The `LoadContext::load_direct` almost does this except it loads the asset from an asset path. We would instead need a way to load an asset from an `AsyncRead` impl instead.

Perhaps an API for this could look like this in `LoadContext`:

```rs
pub async fn load_direct_from_reader<'b>(
    &mut self,
    reader: &'a mut Reader,
    meta_file_reader: Option<&'a mut Reader>,
    path: impl Into<AssetPath<'b>>,
) -> Result<ErasedLoadedAsset, LoadDirectError> {
}
```
I indeed had this exact issue, I'd help implement it if I wasn't so busy but I did want to drop my 2cents that it is a desirable feature.

review_comments: What about a `load_with_reader`, and `load_with_reader_and_settings`? Looking at the `load` and `load_with_settings`, I think it should be possible to build on top of `load_direct_with_reader` and IMO would be disproportionately useful.

I've attempted to create these methods on `LoadContext`, but that required creating matching methods on `AssetServer` to have consistent behaviour. This still doesn't make any breaking changes, but there's now substantially more changes. Additionally, I believe there's a new foot-gun where if a user calls `load_with_reader` but `should_load_dependencies` is `false`. I don't think it makes sense to pass a `Reader` to a loader, only for it to be dropped, but maybe there are cases where you'd want to do that? I've added an `error!` message for now just to flag it for review from you guys.
